insights.title: The summer the salary cap broke: 12 defining signings, $218M for 30.6 win shares
insights.tldr: When the cap jumped 34% in one summer, teams bid against the new money — not production. Chandler Parsons' $22.1M bought 0.2 win shares.
insights.lede: The 12 defining free-agent signings of summer 2016, first-year salary vs. 2016-17 win shares, era-adjusted. Only Ryan Anderson cleared the bar.

insights.foot: Salaries: HoopsRumors top-50 2016-17 + Spotrac cap hits. Cap jumped $70.0M → $94.143M (July 2016). WS from Basketball-Reference.
insights.og_title: The summer the NBA salary cap broke: $218M for 30.6 win shares
insights.og_desc: Twelve teams spent $218.4M on the summer-2016 free-agent class. It bought 30.6 win shares — barely twice LeBron's total, for 7× his salary.
insights.but: But — win shares aren't dollars: this measures production per dollar, not whether the signing was defensible on the day. It would fall apart if Basketball-Reference's win shares systematically undercount 2016-17 role players.

insights.title: The most expensive seats in basketball: $115M for zero games
insights.tldr: John Wall ($44.3M) sat out 2021-22 entirely. Kawhi Leonard ($39.3M) missed it with a torn ACL. In today's cap dollars: $115M for zero win shares.
insights.lede: 2021-22 top-10 salaries: cap-adjusted dollars paid per win share produced. DNP rows are the full adjusted salary for zero production.
insights.stat_label: cap-adjusted $M paid for zero 2021-22 games (Wall + Kawhi)
insights.viz_label: Cap-adjusted $M paid per win share, 2021-22 top-10 (DNP = all of it, zero WS)
insights.foot: Top-10 salaries, 2021-22 season. WS/VORP/MP from Basketball-Reference; salaries cross-checked vs HoopsHype. Adj = salary ÷ $112.4M cap × $154.647M.
insights.og_title: Paid to not play: $115M in cap-adjusted dollars for zero games
insights.og_desc: John Wall and Kawhi Leonard combined for zero 2021-22 games on $83.7M in salary — $115M in today's cap dollars.
insights.but: But — not all of it is waste: Kawhi's absence was a torn ACL, not a choice, and guaranteed contracts make this the price of doing business. This card says what the money bought, not that anyone should have known.

insights.title: The cheat code: the very top of the pay scale is usually a bargain
insights.tldr: James Harden's 2016-17 ($26.5M → 15.0 WS) cost $2.9M per win share in today's dollars. Eight of the ten best-value seasons are top-5 salaries — true superstars outproduce even max money.
insights.lede: Best era-adjusted dollars-per-win-share among top-10 salaries, 6 matched seasons, minimum 5 win shares.
insights.stat_label: cap-adjusted $M per win share — James Harden '16-17, best in panel
insights.viz_label: Cap-adjusted $M paid per win share (lower = better), min 5 WS
insights.foot: Panel: top-10 salaries × 6 seasons, Basketball-Reference WS. Era-adjusted to the 2025-26 $154.647M cap.
insights.og_title: The NBA cheat code: max money for superstars is usually a bargain
insights.og_desc: Harden '16-17 cost $2.9M per win share in today's cap dollars. The dead zone isn't the top of the pay scale — it's ranks 8-15.
insights.but: But — the 5-win-share floor screens out the true top-of-the-pay-scale busts; this ranks the best top-10 seasons, not all of them. A lower salary band (ranks 11–30) with better $/win-share seasons would break the 'cheat code' claim.

insights.foot: 12 qualifying moves, ΔUSG ≥ 4.0, 1999-00 → 2024-25. Pre = final pre-move season meeting the stardom bar (All-Star or 25+ USG or 20+ PPG or 8+ WS) on a team that won ≤1 playoff round. Post = first season with the new team. Team rounds from the public record; full methodology in research/invisible-stardom-FINDINGS.md.
insights.lede: Stars who shrank for a contender: Jrue Holiday gave up 8.7 points of usage rate and won a ring. Malone, Harden, Payton gave up as much and lost. Rings cluster where the star joined an already-elite core.
insights.og_desc: Jrue Holiday gave up 8.7 points of usage rate going from Milwaukee All-Star to Boston's fourth option — and won a ring. 12 invisible-stardom sacrifices, ranked.
insights.stat_label: Jrue Holiday's usage drop, Milwaukee All-Star to Boston's fourth option — the biggest invisible sacrifice, and a ring
insights.title: The biggest sacrifices nobody saw
insights.tldr: Lottery-team stars who shrank for a contender: Jrue Holiday gave up 8.7 points of usage rate and won a ring, but Malone, Harden and Payton gave up as much and lost — rings went to the stars who joined already-elite cores.
insights.but: But — correlation isn't the recipe: joining an already-elite core is easier to measure than whether the sacrifice caused the ring. The 12 qualifying moves are the ones we could verify — the dataset only covers what the ledger can see.

insights.foot: Love: '13-14 MIN (26.1 PPG, 28.8 USG, 14.0 WS) → '14-15 CLE. Bosh: '09-10 TOR (24.0 PPG, 28.7 USG, 10.1 WS) → '10-11 MIA. Both All-Stars on non-playoff teams; both won rings. Data: Basketball-Reference, scraped 2026-10-01.
insights.lede: Same archetype, different economics. Kevin Love's win shares fell off a cliff (14.0 → 8.4) — real production surrendered, and it took two years to make the fit work. Chris Bosh's win shares rose (10.1 → 10.8) — he gave up shots, not wins, because the team around him was better. Two ways to disappear for a ring.
insights.og_desc: Love gave up 5.6 win shares for a ring; Bosh gave up 5.3 points a game and his win shares went up. Two kinds of sacrifice.
insights.og_title: Love gave up wins. Bosh gave up shots.

insights.stat_label: Win shares Love gave up, Minnesota to Cleveland. Bosh's went up.
insights.title: Two ways to disappear for a ring
insights.tldr: Kevin Love gave up 5.6 win shares going from Minnesota's everything to Cleveland's third wheel. Chris Bosh gave up 5.3 points a game — and his win shares rose. Same archetype, different economics.
insights.viz_label: What each star gave up (negative = surrendered)
insights.but: But — two players isn't a pattern: this is a case study in fit, not a rule. It would fall apart if Bosh's win-share rise was driven by LeBron and Wade's gravity rather than his own adjustment.

insights.foot: 7 players. Peak = best 3-consecutive-season USG% on the same team, before the title window. Parker is approximate: 2008-09 single-season peak vs window average, intervening years unknown. Regular-season USG%; Basketball-Reference, 2026-10-01.
insights.lede: Role drop measured against each player's own same-team peak — the lens the team-switch cards can't see. Manu Ginobili never had a peak to drop from: 349 starts in 1,019 games, peaking at 28.7 USG% as a sixth man while posting .240+ win shares per 48 — a starter with that production plays 32-34%.
insights.og_desc: Wade surrendered 4.6 usage points in his prime and won two rings. Manu never took the big role at all.
insights.og_title: The biggest NBA role shrinks happened without changing teams
insights.stat_label: usage points Wade surrendered in his prime, ages 29-32 — and won 2 titles
insights.title: The biggest role shrinks in NBA history happened without changing teams
insights.tldr: The storied sacrifices never switched teams — Wade ceded the Heat in his prime, Manu took the bench for a dynasty, Duncan shrank at 38.

insights.but: But — regular-season usage isn't the whole role: playoff minutes and defensive assignments shifted too. Parker is approximate: 2008-09 single-season peak vs window average, intervening years unknown.

insights.foot: 4 documented pay cuts. Documented minimums from reporting, not exact counterfactuals. Salaries: Spotrac cash. Reporting: ESPN (Stein, MacMahon), HoopsRumors, NBC Sports, Basketball Network, Pounding The Rock, 2026-10-01. Three zero rows folded into this footnote: Parker's discount was real but unquantifiable; Klay (full max 2019) and Curry (full supermax) took no discount.
insights.lede: Dirk's 2010 discount funded the Tyson Chandler trade that anchored the 2011 title; Duncan's 2012 halving kept Diaw, Green and Mills for 2014. These pay cuts have receipts — and rings attached.
insights.og_desc: Dirk left ~$46M documented on the table; Duncan ~$35M+. Both discounts bought championships.
insights.og_title: The hometown discount leaderboard: millions left, rings won
insights.stat_label: documented $M Dirk Nowitzki left on the table — his 2010 discount bought the 2011 title
insights.title: The hometown discount: salary left on the table, rings won
insights.tldr: Dirk left ~$46M and Duncan ~$35M+ documented on the table — and both discounts are directly tied to championships.
insights.but: But — 'documented minimums' are floors, not totals: the real discounts were likely bigger, and the counterfactual max offers are reported, not offered. If the reported offers weren't real, the leaderboard moves.
